verses.zh: （大卫的记念诗，交与伶长。）　神啊，求你快快搭救我！耶和华啊，求你速速帮助我！
verses.en: For the music director, by David; written to get God’s attention.[NOTE:1] O God, please be willing to rescue me.[NOTE:2] O Lord, hurry and help me.[NOTE:3]
notes: Psalm 70. This psalm is almost identical to Ps 40:13-17. The psalmist asks for God’s help and for divine retribution against his enemies.

Heb “to cause to remember.” The same form, a Hiphil infinitive of זָכַר (zakhar, “remember”), also appears in the superscription of Ps 38. Some understand this in the sense of “for the memorial offering,” but it may carry the idea of bringing one’s plight to God’s attention (see P. C. Craigie, Psalms 1-50 [WBC], 303).
Heb “O God, to rescue me.” A main verb is obviously missing. The verb רָצָה (ratsah, “be willing”) should be supplied (see Ps 40:13). Ps 40:13 uses the divine name “Lord” rather than “God.”
verses.commentary:
70:1 The NASB assumes the Qal IMPERATIVE is used twice (cf. Ps. 22:19; 38:22;
40:13; 71:12; 141:1) and has parallel OBJECTS (cf. Ps. 70:5).

- deliver me

- help me

Also notice that God (Elohim) is parallel to Lord
(YHWH), as they are in verse 5.

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, C., D.

verses.zh: 愿那些寻索我命的，抱愧蒙羞；愿那些喜悦我遭害的，退后受辱。
verses.en: May those who are trying to take my lifebe embarrassed and ashamed.[NOTE:1] May those who want to harm mebe turned back and ashamed.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “hurry to my help.” See Pss 22:19; 38:22.
Heb “may they be embarrassed and ashamed, the ones seeking my life.” Ps 40:14 has “together” after “ashamed,” and “to snatch it away” after “my life.”
verses.commentary:
70:2 "Let. . ." This is the
English way to denote the JUSSIVE OF REQUEST.
See Contextual Insights, B.

▣ "seek" This VERBAL (BDB 134, KB 152, Piel
PARTICIPLE) occurs in Ps. 70:2 and 4. It describes two kinds of people.

- those who seek to kill or hurt others to get their way (cf. Ps. 37:32; 71:13,24)

- those who seek God (cf. Ps. 24:6; 27:8; 40:16; 69:6; 70:4)

70:2-3 "Who. . ." Those who oppose
the psalmist are characterized in three parallel phrases.

- who seek my life (lit. nephesh; see
SPECIAL TOPIC: NEPHESH)

- who delight in my hurt

- who say, "Aha, aha"

This denotes a common OT literary technique called "reversal."
What they wished to happen to the godly psalmist, happens to them!

verses.zh: 愿那些对我说阿哈、阿哈的，因羞愧退后。
verses.en: May those who say, “Aha! Aha!”be driven back[NOTE:1] and disgraced.[NOTE:2]
notes: See Ps 35:4 for a similar prayer.tn The four prefixed verbal forms in this verse are understood as jussives. The psalmist is calling judgment down on his enemies.
The prefixed verbal form is understood as a jussive in this imprecation.
verses.commentary:
70:3 "shame" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: SHAME

REB

This Hebrew INTERROGATIVE (BDB 210) usually denotes
satisfaction over an enemy's misfortune (cf. Ps. 35:21,25; 40:15; Ezek. 25:3; 26:2; 36:2).

verses.zh: 愿一切寻求你的，因你高兴欢喜；愿那些喜爱你救恩的，常说：当尊　神为大！
verses.en: May all those who seek you be happy and rejoice in you.May those who love to experience[NOTE:1] your deliverance say continually,[NOTE:2] “May God[NOTE:3] be praised!”[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “May they be turned back according to their shame, those who say, ‘Aha! Aha!’” Ps 40:15 has the verb “humiliated” instead of “turned back” and adds “to me” after “say.”
Heb “those who love,” which stands metonymically for its cause, the experience of being delivered by God.
The three prefixed verbal forms prior to the quotation are understood as jussives. The psalmist balances out his imprecation against his enemies with a prayer of blessing on the godly.
Ps 40:16 uses the divine name “Lord” here instead of “God.”
verses.commentary:
70:4 "seek You" This is an OT idiom for a personal faith relationship
with God characterized by

- temple worship (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: WORSHIP)

- covenant obedience

The last line of Ps. 70:4 may be temple liturgy. See note at v. 2.

▣ "love" This word for "love" (BDB 12, KB 17, Qal PARTICIPLE)
is one of several Hebrew words translated in the LXX by agapeō.

SPECIAL TOPIC: LOVE

▣ "salvation" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: SALVATION (OT)

▣

NASB, NKJV, Peshitta, LXX
"Let God be magnified"

NJB, NRSV
"God is great"

REB
"All glory to God!"

JPSOA
"Extolled be God!"

The MT has "God (Elohim) is great." The VERB (BDB 152, KB 178) is a Qal
IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense. This is a recognition of YHWH's

- self ‒ 2 Sam. 7:22; Ps. 35:27; 40:16; 104:1; Mal. 1:5

- name ‒ 2 Sam. 7:25

- Messiah ‒ Micah 5:4

verses.zh: 但我是困苦穷乏的；　神啊，求你速速到我这里来！你是帮助我的，搭救我的。耶和华啊，求你不要耽延！
verses.en: I am oppressed and needy.[NOTE:1] O God, hurry to me.[NOTE:2] You are my helper and my deliverer.O Lord,[NOTE:3] do not delay.
notes: The prefixed verbal form is taken as a jussive, “may the Lord be magnified [in praise].” Another option is to take the verb as an imperfect, “the Lord is great.” See Ps 35:27.
Ps 40:17 has “may the Lord pay attention to me.”
verses.commentary:
70:5 Notice that the two concepts of "deliver"
and "help" of Ps. 70:1 are repeated (different but synonymous
VERB for "deliver").

▣ "I am afflicted and needy"
The psalmist characterizes his own perceived situation. God is great (Ps.
70:4) but he is hurting. He entreats God to come to his aid quickly.

Both of the most common names for Israel's Deity appear in this verse. They are in one
sense synonymous, but have unique aspects.

This is a study guide commentary, which
means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare
your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is
the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every
paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- Notice the Qal IMPERATIVE "hasten" (BDB 301, KB 300) opens
(cf. Ps. 70:1b) and closes (cf. Ps. 70:5b) the Psalm (i.e., inclusio). This VERB
is repeated in Psalm 22:19; 38:22; 40:13,17; 71:12.

- Notice the number of IMPERFECTS used as JUSSIVES
(note the parallelism).

- Negative

- let those be ashamed, Ps. 70:2a – BDB 101, KB 116, Qal
IMPERFECT, cf. Ps. 35:4; 83:17

- let those be humiliated, Ps. 70:2a – BDB 344, KB 340, Qal
IMPERFECT, cf. Ps. 40:14

- let those be turned back, Ps. 70:2c – BDB 690, KB 744,
Niphal IMPERFECT

- let those be dishonored, Ps. 70:2c – BDB 483, KB 480, Niphal
IMPERFECT

- let those be turned back, Ps. 70:3a – BDB 996, KB 1427, Qal
IMPERFECT

- Positive

- let all who seek You rejoice, Ps. 70:4 – BDB 965, KB 1314, Qal
IMPERFECT

- let all who seek You be glad, Ps. 70:4 – BDB 970, KB 1333, Qal
IMPERFECT

- let those who love Your salvation say. . .," Ps. 70:4b – BDB 55,
KB 65, Qal IMPERFECT

- God be magnified, Ps. 70:4c – BDB 152, KB 178, Qal
IMPERFECT

- do not delay, Ps. 70:5d – BDB 28, KB 34, Piel
IMPERFECT

- Notice the wonderful synonymous parallelism of the Psalm.

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEBREW POETLRY

- This Psalm is repeated with some differences in Psalm 40:13-17, except for Ps. 70:3a.

- Psalm 70:3, "turn back" (BDB 690 I)

- Psalm 40:15, "appalled" (BDB 1030)

Remember, moderns do not know the when, who, or how of the transmission
of OT books. There were obviously editors and compilers involved over a long period
of time. We assume that these were as inspired as the original author.
